title: docs(qa): the share-link landing page asserts the 'Sign in required' state for a signed_in link (#23169)
body:
Part of #23169
Clause-②: no (QA data)

This PR lands one row of #23169: `access-security.share-link-landing-page` C3, from QA run #23163 (`surface:browser`). The row waited for PR #23222, which also edited `access-security.json`; it merged as `66949b7729`. #23169 remains open for its other row, `platform-core.lifecycle-retention-sweep` steps[4], which still waits on a maintainer ruling and is not part of this PR.

## What changed

One item changes: `access-security.share-link-landing-page`, at `.items[27]` of `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json`. Its `revision` goes from 1 to 2, and one `history` entry is appended. Indices are zero-based.

| field | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `fixtures.knownGaps[2]` | the page folds every 401 into the password prompt, so a `signed_in` link opened anonymously renders "Password required". It asked to be revised once the console told the two codes apart | a regression row, expected PASS. The page reads a 401 by its `error.code`, and a `signed_in` link opened anonymously renders the "Sign in required" state. It names the objectui pins |
| `acceptance[3].clause` (the item's clause 4) | no leak, plus "a designed state", recording whichever state renders | asserts the sign-in state: the "Sign in required" heading, "The owner shared this link with signed-in users only.", and a Sign in link to the console's `/login` route that redirects back. Never the password prompt or a password input |
| `acceptance[3].verify` | "the rendered state noted" | the record-free `401 SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` body, then a screenshot and a DOM read of the sign-in state |
| `variants[5]` | "refused, designed state" | "refused: the 'Sign in required' state, no password prompt" |

No other item changes, and no other field of this item. This is the same edit discipline as PR #23278.

## How the row was checked

The row was re-checked from source. No browser was driven and no app was booted, as in PR #23278. QA run #23163 saw the state live, at objectstack `36b2889c` with objectui `1fb1ced36243`: "`signed_in` audience renders a dedicated 'Sign in required' state (401 SIGN_IN_REQUIRED), member 200".

- **Console, objectui at `1fb1ced36243`,** still `main`'s `.objectui-sha`:
  - `apps/console/src/pages/SharedRecordPage.tsx`: `fetchResolve` reads a 401's body through `resolveGateOf`. A `sign-in-required` answer sets the `sign-in` gate. That gate renders "Sign in required", "The owner shared this link with signed-in users only." and a Sign in link to `/login` whose `redirect` is the router path.
  - `apps/console/src/pages/shared-record-shape.ts`: `RESOLVE_GATE_BY_CODE` maps `NEEDS_PASSWORD` and `WRONG_PASSWORD` to the password gate and `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` to the sign-in gate. Any other code names no gate, and the page shows the server's message.
  - Pins at the same revision: `SharedRecordPage-11649.test.tsx` ("shows the sign-in path back to this link, and no password prompt") and `shared-record-shape.test.ts` ("reads each 401 code as its gate").
- **Framework, at base `87e902dcbb`:** both resolve mounts answer `401 SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` when a live `signed_in` link without a password is opened anonymously. One is the probe in the resolve route of `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-routes.ts`; the other is its dispatcher twin in `packages/runtime/src/domains/share-links.ts`.

The two sides agree. So, as the item itself asked, the knownGap becomes a regression row and clause 4 becomes an assertion.

**Edit discipline.** One scripted edit:

- Each replacement asserted that its anchor occurs exactly once inside the item and exactly once in the file.
- After the save, the script parsed the file and checked it against the base blob:
  - the 27 other items are identical;
  - this item changed only in `revision`, `fixtures`, `acceptance`, `variants` and `history`;
  - inside those fields, only knownGaps[2], acceptance[3].clause, acceptance[3].verify and variants[5] differ;
  - `revision` went up by one, and `history` is the base list plus one entry.
- The new text cites code by function and string names, never by line number. The ledger's anchor rule (`scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs`) says a line number is not an anchor form.

The eighth is the attachments-storage anchor floor. The daily watchdog owns them.

- **The selector still reads the item:** `node scripts/checklist-select.mjs access-security.share-link-landing-page` prints `1 runnable item(s)`.

## Acceptance notes

Two things are noted here and not filed by this PR.

1. **A related product defect, out of scope and reproduced (handed to the seat to file).** A link minted with both a password and `audience: 'signed_in'`, opened anonymously with the correct password, answers `401 WRONG_PASSWORD`.
   - Measured with a throwaway probe, not committed. It drove plugin-sharing's real resolve route on a real `SqlDriver` (`:memory:`):
     - no password: `401 NEEDS_PASSWORD`;
     - wrong password: `401 WRONG_PASSWORD`;
     - correct password: `401 WRONG_PASSWORD`;
     - signed in, correct password: `200`.
   - Why: `resolveToken` refuses on the audience before it checks the password. The route's probe then answers from the row in password-first order, and it reads only whether a password was sent, not whether it was right. The dispatcher twin has the same order (source read).
   - Who can produce it: objectui's `ShareDialog.tsx` at the pin sends an audience and a password in one create. The landing page then says "Wrong password." for the right one, and never offers sign-in.
   - This item mints its password token and its `signed_in` token separately, so it does not reach that case.
2. **Stale line ranges in this item's untouched fields.** `acceptance[1].verify` (`SharedRecordPage.tsx,143-176`), `acceptance[2].verify` (`,178-186`), `knownGaps[1]` and `source[1]` (`,190-234`) no longer point at those code paths at the pin.
   - They are not fixed here. The anchor rule judges `file:line`, but not this comma spelling, which appears 44 times across `areas/*.json`.
   - Re-pointing them by name is a re-authoring of the item, not this row.
